style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: matte clay 3D render of a modular mechanical measurement assembly on a weathered concrete surface. Split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast. On the left, a cleanly engineered gauge housing with its needle surging high; on the right, a matching gauge with its needle dropping low. Crafted with matte surfaces, moulding seams, and heavy contact shadows. One directional key light raking across the concrete, muted matte palette, generous negative space. No text, no moulded lettering, no bare geometry.
negative_prompt: text, letters, words, garbled text, watermark, typography, UI elements
rationale: Clay render perfectly captures the abstract structural disparity of software benchmarks by turning the 75-point gap into a tangible, minimalist mechanical assembly of dual gauges.
subject: dual mechanical gauges showing contrasting extreme measurements
core_thesis: The published randomized trials of AI coding tools span 55.8% faster to 19% slower, so a seat count has to rest on a trial of your own code.
core_conflict: Vendor-supplied greenfield speed benchmarks versus the reality of maintaining known, complex proprietary code.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast
